question: ________ delegates from all over the country congregated for the first session of the Indian National Congress at Bombay in December 1885.
solution:
The correct answer is __**72**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The first session of the Indian National Congress was held in Bombay (now Mumbai) in December 1885.
 
• 72 delegates from different parts of India participated in this historic session.
 
• The session was presided over by Womesh Chunder Bonnerjee, a prominent lawyer and one of the founding members of the Congress.
 
• The primary aim of the Congress was to obtain a greater share in government for educated Indians and to create a platform for civic and political dialogue among the Indian populace.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Indian National Congress (INC)**

 
 
• The Indian National Congress was founded on December 28, 1885, by Allan Octavian Hume, Dadabhai Naoroji, and Dinshaw Wacha.
 
• The INC played a significant role in the Indian independence movement against British rule.
 
• The Congress initially sought reform within the British government but gradually moved towards demanding full independence.
 
• Prominent leaders such as Mahatma Gandhi, Jawaharlal Nehru, and Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel emerged from the Congress during the freedom struggle.
 
 
 
• **Womesh Chunder Bonnerjee**
 
 
• Womesh Chunder Bonnerjee was a distinguished lawyer and the first president of the Indian National Congress.
 
• He presided over the first session of the Congress held in Bombay in December 1885.
 
• Bonnerjee was a key figure in the early days of the Congress and contributed significantly to its establishment and growth.
 
 
 
• **Allan Octavian Hume**
 
 
• Allan Octavian Hume was a British civil servant and one of the founders of the Indian National Congress.
 
• Hume played a crucial role in bringing together Indian leaders to form a political platform for voicing their grievances and demands.
 
• He is often referred to as the "Father of the Indian National Congress."
 
 
 
• **Objectives of the Indian National Congress**
 
 
• The initial objectives of the INC included promoting friendly relations between nationalist political workers from different parts of the country.
 
• The Congress aimed to develop and consolidate the feelings of national unity irrespective of caste, religion, or province.
 
• It sought to formulate popular demands and present them to the British government in a systematic manner.
 
• The INC also worked towards training and organizing public opinion in the country.
